document_flags: All courses in programmes 17-23 carry Status C (Core); the source defines no E-status elective courses for these programmes.
P9b (UTME subject combinations) marked NOT FOUND for these programmes in the source metadata.

Course titles were taken from each programme's P13/P14 Learning Outcomes/Course Contents headings; units/LH/PH from the '(N Units C: LH x; PH y)' annotations. Where an annotation gives only LH, PH is recorded as null.

PIM (17): AMS 101-104 are absent from the PIM 100L table (unique among all programmes); PIM 310, 312, 412, 413, 414 appear in the LO section only, not in the course table; PIM 202 carries an ENT 202 prefix error in source.
PRM (18): PRM 408 has no learning outcomes/course contents/title in source.
PMG (19): source uses 'PGM' prefix in some LO headings vs 'PMG' in the table; PMG 424 listed as 4 units in P12 table but 6 Units in the LO heading.

PAD (20): the P12 token 'PAD409-Project(6)' conflicts with the LO section, where PAD 406 is the 6-unit Research Project and PAD 409 is a 2-unit course; several PAD courses show unit/LH discrepancies between the P12 table and LO headings (flagged per course).
SIM (21): SIM 312/322/323/324 shown as 3 units but LH 30 (inconsistent); SIM 311/321/412/422 show table-vs-LO unit conflicts (flagged per course).

TAX (22): 100L has a duplicate table variant in source (12 units, no ACC); TAX 311 code is used for two different courses; ACC 101/ACC 102 have no LO entry within the Taxation section (titles null); TAX 411/421 share a combined 6-unit project title in source.
TPM (23): GST 111 LH/PH reversed (45/15) in source 100L table; GST 312 appears twice in the 300L LO section; TPM 400/401 is a combined code with the LO section covering only TPM 400.

programmes.name: Business Administration
employability_skills: communication: Both oral, written communication and listening skills; Business Administration graduates would be clear, concise and focused in their interactions and engagement;
teamwork: Graduates of Business Administration should demonstrate the ability to build positive working relationships that assist each team member to achieve business objectives;

problem solving: From a variety of courses offered on business decision, graduate should demonstrate the ability to implement logical and analytical approach to solve problems and resolve organizational conflicts and issues;

leadership: Graduates of this programme should demonstrate ability to influence and motivate teams and other members of staff to achieve organizational goals and objective through assigning responsibilities and delegating tasks to achieve results;

entrepreneurial skills: Spotting gaps in the market, suggesting ways to improve processes, or coming up with new ideas are all signs of an entrepreneurial approach; You don't have to set up your own business to make use of your enterprise skills; Many employers will be looking out for graduate recruits with these qualities;

lT skills: Students of business administration are empowered with critical IT skills with which they can demonstrate to employers their versatility in the use of different management software applications to enrich the work experience;
resilience: Graduates of this programme would be imbued with resilience quality which will enable them to cope with changes, problems and stress in the work place; and

analytical skills: Managers work with different kinds of information, patterns and trends from which they must draw meaningful conclusions. Hence, relevant courses build into the students' analytical skills.

leadership: Graduates of this programme should demonstrate ability to influence and motivate teams and other members of staff to achieve organizational goals and objective through assigning responsibilities and delegating tasks to achieve results

lT skills: Students of business administration are empowered with critical IT skills with which they can demonstrate to employers their versatility in the use of different management software applications to enrich the work experience
resilience: Graduates of this programme would be imbued with resilience quality which will enable them to cope with changes, problems and stress in the work place; and

analytical skills: Managers work with different kinds of information, patterns and trends from which they must draw meaningful conclusions. Hence, relevant courses build into the students' analytical skills

courses.title: Entrepreneurial Financing

exhibit attitude that promotes self-reliance;
develop the desire for financial independence;

courses.content_summary: Concept and theories of entrepreneurship and innovation; nature and types of entrepreneurships; characteristics of entrepreneurs; risk-taking behavior; innovation and entrepreneurship development processes; basic processes of starting an enterprise.

courses.title: Entrepreneurial Environment
skills_learned: spot opportunities in the Nigerian key economic sectors;
appreciate environmental challenges facing new ventures; and
identify ways of overcoming binding constraints to businesses.
courses.content_summary: External environmental factors affecting entrepreneurs and entrepreneurship development (socio-cultural, economic, political, environmental, technological, global, competitive); proactive and responsive measures to deal with the changing entrepreneurial environment.

courses.title: Marketing for New Ventures
skills_learned: appreciate the world of money and how to stay liquid to avoid financial embarrassments;
develop savings and investments culture using legitimate means;
be exposed to commodity and money markets where money circulates;
appreciate inherent risks in financial transactions and how to mitigate/hedge financial risks; and
describe unethical practices in financial dealings and how to avoid illegal financial activities.
courses.content_summary: Personal cash build up (savings); creating cash flow; types of investment; investing in stock and commodity markets; financial market instruments; insurance and risk hedging; tax issues; online financial opportunities (bitcoin, crowd funding) and risks; safeguarding against online fraud, money laundering, etc.

courses.title: Theories of Entrepreneurship
skills_learned: analyse the statistical tools needed for measuring business performance;
apply knowledge of statistics to business performance; and

courses.content_summary: Nature of statistics; statistical inquiries; basic concepts; variables; data sources and collection; presentation of data; measures of central tendency and dispersion; probability distributions; sampling theory; hypothesis testing; chi-square; linear regression; correlation; index numbers; time series analysis.

exchange entrepreneurial ideas with captains of industry; and
engage with mentors and receive handholding by entrepreneurs.
courses.content_summary: Industrial Learning and Tours I (mapped to ENT 232). Practical exposure to entrepreneurship and business management through industry learning/excursion and/or foreign study tours; first-hand learning from entrepreneurs; group paper submitted at the end.

New business development: business planning, market research, etc. Entrepreneurial finance: venture capital, equity finance. Micro finance, personal savings,

courses.title: Business Opportunity Scouting
skills_learned: spot diverse opportunities in the environment;
appreciate opportunities in e-commerce;
identify a viable business opportunity; and
perform proof of concept and demonstrate market potential.
courses.content_summary: Business Opportunity Scouting (mapped to ENT 315). Sources of business opportunities; difference between ideas and opportunities; strategies for scanning and evaluating opportunities; trend analysis; sector scan; deep dives; mentorship and handholding.

courses.title: Sociology of Entrepreneurship
skills_learned: appreciate the social factors/institutions that influence the entrepreneurship;
describe specific constraints of entrepreneurship in a traditional/ developing society; and
explain entrepreneurial traits and value orientations.
courses.content_summary: Sociology of Entrepreneurship (mapped to ENT 323). Sociological entrepreneurship theory; social profile of the entrepreneur; determinants of entrepreneurial personality; entrepreneurship, poverty and unemployment; social enablers; constraints; creating entrepreneurial society.

courses.title: Small Scale Business Management
skills_learned: analyse the importance of small business in achieving inclusive growth in the society;
appreciate the requirements for establishing and managing micro and small enterprises;
describe how to avoid business failures at start up stage; and
appreciate how to manage transition to growth.
courses.content_summary: Small Scale Business Management (mapped to ENT 325). Roles of small business in the Nigerian economy; definition and characteristics; financial and administrative control; setting up small business and legal requirements; principles of managing small business; startup challenges.

courses.title: Family Business & Succession Planning
skills_learned: explain the relevance and importance of family ventures;
describe the challenges of initiating and running family ventures in a traditional society;
appreciate the key success factors for managing family businesses; and
demonstrate how traditional ventures can be transformed into global brands.
courses.content_summary: Family Business and Succession Planning (mapped to ENT 328). Successful national and global family-controlled businesses; concept and types of family business; characteristics; challenges; succession difficulties (conflicts, poor management, over personalization of fortune and assets).

courses.title: Feasibilities and Business Planning
skills_learned: analyze business viability using tried and testing models;
prepare and pitch a bankable business plan for lenders and potential investors; and
develop a disciplined approach to implementing business plans.
courses.content_summary: Feasibilities and Business Planning (mapped to ENT 332). Elements of professionally written feasibility studies and business plans; project appraisal before investment; project evaluation techniques (ARR, PBP, NPV, IRR, PI).

courses.title: Research Methods
skills_learned: conduct basic research and perform business surveys;
analyse and interpret research findings; and
deploy relevant research findings and recommendations in business and management.
courses.content_summary: Research Methods (mapped to ENT 334). Scientific investigation; information gathering, analysis and interpretation; problem identification; data collection techniques; tools for analysis and report writing; marketing research; feasibility studies; business case development.

courses.title: Industrial Learning and Tours II
skills_learned: appreciate the dynamics of entrepreneurial environment;
interact with practitioners, customers, suppliers, stakeholders/ shareholders to generate real life experience; and
enable students obtain mentorship and build relationships.
courses.content_summary: Industrial Learning and Tours II (mapped to ENT 336). Individual study of a specific IT-oriented entrepreneurial venture; technical/project report on its mission, products, processes, markets, customers, supply chain, challenges and opportunities, prepared with industry practitioner support.

courses.title: Social Entrepreneurship & Comm. Dev.
skills_learned: describe ventures that are socially relevant;
explain social entrepreneurial attitude; and
demonstrate how to fix identified challenges and needs in the community/society.
courses.content_summary: Social Entrepreneurship and Community Development (mapped to ENT 416). Innovative concepts, practices and strategies of social entrepreneurship; fund raising for social projects; NGOs and civil societies; creating social enterprises for jobs and well-being of the less privileged.

courses.title: Technological Entrepreneurship & IPR
skills_learned: describe how original products, ideas, and concepts are developed;
explain dimensions of technological innovations and how they enhance competitiveness;
apply administrative, business and legal processes in order to protect their innovation from the risk of piracy; and
analyze profitable market and innovations.
courses.content_summary: Technological Entrepreneurship and Intellectual Property Rights (mapped to ENT 417). Creative process for high-tech ventures; entrepreneurship theory and practice for technology-based enterprises; intellectual property and its protection; Nigerian copyrights laws; protecting original ideas from piracy.

courses.title: Management of Creativity & Innovation
skills_learned: appreciate their unique talents and how to think differently;
be exposed to multi-dimensions of innovation;
explain doing things differently in the business arena; and
become prepared to succeed in the highly competitive world of business.
courses.content_summary: Management of Creativity and Innovation (mapped to ENT 424). Creativity and creative processes; how the human mind works; environmental factors influencing creative thinking; concept, theories, nature and types of innovation; strategies for financing innovation.

courses.title: E-Business
skills_learned: explain modern business transitions and how to reach global market;
demonstrate how businesses are operated using e-commerce platform; and
explain use of information and communication technology to network and build alliances.
courses.content_summary: E-Business (mapped to ENT 427). Concept definitions; overview of internet and mobile telecommunication; importance of e-business; website design; internet advertisements; competitive advantage via e-adverts; online sales; e-payments; bitcoin; crowd funding.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship and Gender Issues
skills_learned: appreciate the positive role of women in the socio-economic development of society;
be exposed to binding constraints to women social and economic empowerment; and
demonstrate an approach — social or economic enterprise, to help in reducing gender gap in their localities.
courses.content_summary: Entrepreneurship and Gender Issues (mapped to ENT 428). Gender as a factor in entrepreneurship; gender theories; place of women in entrepreneurship; binding constraints to women entrepreneurship in Nigeria; gender policy; women empowerment strategies.

courses.title: Strategic Thinking & Negotiation Skills
skills_learned: describe critical thinking and become ready to challenge status quo;
explain negotiation and approaches to innovative problem solving;
identify techniques for innovative solution; and
implement business dealings in a professional manner.
courses.content_summary: Strategic Thinking, Problem Solving and Negotiation Skills (mapped to ENT 429). Traditional (horizontal) thinking process; lateral thinking perspective; analysis of views about thinking; problem solving and negotiation skills.

courses.title: Risk Management and Insurance
skills_learned: appreciate the inherent nature and types of business risks;
analyze acceptable risks based on risk classifications;
appreciate the role of insurance in mitigating business risks; and
describe major categories of insurance policies.
courses.content_summary: Risk Management and Insurance (mapped to ENT 432). Nature and classifications of risks; risk analysis tools; risk management techniques; scope and schemes of insurance; classification of insurance; insurance contracts; social insurance and pension schemes; insurance markets.

courses.title: Research for Enterprise
skills_learned: develop viable business concept that fit his/her interest;
develop prototype, or bankable business plan; and
explain business concept, incubation and pitching for funding.
courses.content_summary: Research for Enterprise (mapped to ENT 442). Practical project working with an entrepreneurship development center or innovation hub to search or prove a business idea, new product or market and develop it into an actual venture; report of not less than 2,000 words.
